- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 1–3% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price starts declining, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–10 day average.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong negative sentiment; if sentiment rebounds to 0.67+, forecast should not immediately revert to prior peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply mild downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often ignores trend persistence; align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- When sentiment is high and price is near historical highs, model tends to overestimate; cap forecast at 10% above recent 10-day high if sentiment >0.7.
